results.content: With three months to go until the U.S. midterm elections in November, voters increasingly seem to prefer Democrats over the Republican Party that has had control of Congress for the last two years. Results of a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday showed that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate at present, compared to 37% for a Republican. The same survey also found that, for the first time in nearly a decade of its polling series, voters perceive the Democratic Party as having a better plan for the economy than the Republican Party. results.content: President Trump’s approval rating dipped again this week, following a downward trend in support for the president amid the ongoing Iran war and mounting affordability concerns ahead of November’s midterms. The latest survey from The Economist/YouGov, published Monday, found 33 percent of respondents said they approved of how Trump has handled his job as president. Support for the president was split largely along partisan lines, with 79 percent of GOP respondents and only 4 percent of Democratic respondents approving of Trump’s job performance, according to the poll.
